card: This pull request requires a C++23 compiler (GCC 13+ or Clang 19+) across CMake, depends, and CI. It replaces in-tree polyfills like util::Expected and byteswap macros with std::expected and std::byteswap, and applies C++23 features like string::contains across 53 files. The author notes that workarounds to avoid C++23 continue to accumulate while dependencies such as libmultiprocess already rely on C++23 constructs. This RFC is intended to unblock further modernization tracked in #34979.
changed_since_previous: Added an IWYU cleanup commit to adjust include directives for re-exported return types, slightly reducing the file touch count.
evidence: Author description: 'C++23 for Bitcoin Core is mostly a "style update" on top of C++20. However, the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features... so that new stuff is unlocked (linking #34979).'

Diff eliminates 117 lines from `src/util/expected.h`, deletes `src/util/types.h` (`ALWAYS_FALSE`), and replaces 41 lines of conditional compiler builtins in `src/compat/byteswap.h` with `std::byteswap`.
problem: Sticking to C++20 requires maintaining custom polyfills and compatibility shims (such as `util::Expected` and custom byteswap fallback implementations) while preventing the use of standard C++23 library features, even as parts of upstream dependencies like libmultiprocess have begun adopting C++23 syntax.

risk.why: Bumping the minimum compiler version and core language standard affects release binaries, toolchain compatibility, and distribution packaging across all platforms.

scope_notes: This is an experimental RFC marked WIP/nomerge. A substantial portion of the diff consists of mechanical clang-tidy migrations replacing `.find(...) != std::string::npos` with `.contains(...)` across approximately 30 files.
summary: This pull request bumps the project C++ standard requirement from C++20 to C++23 in CMake, depends, and CI configurations, raising minimum supported compiler versions to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It removes internal polyfills for expected values, byteswapping, and static assertions in favor of `std::expected`, `std::byteswap`, and C++23 `static_assert(false)`. It also refactors string search calls across the codebase to use `std::string::contains` and adopts `std::views::zip` in the kernel block import loop.
